decisions.reason: A black-finish variant of existing drains costs little to keep and carries an open upside from the design trend, so the option stays alive while demand is still uncertain.
A shower channel for seamless coverings is close to the core offer, has its own page and fits barrier-free bathroom architecture, so it has a low holding cost and a promising outlook.
The pump-assisted solution is more uncertain and costlier to support, but one year gives too little evidence to abandon it, and it opens access to renovation applications.
A tileable floor drain is a natural extension of the established range, presented on its own page, with minimal incremental cost and solid demand from installers.
A stainless steel design grate uses the firm's own manufacturing and design strength at low marginal cost, so keeping it is clearly worthwhile.
